analysis.title: The AI reckoning: everyone is dumping AI, that's where things get interesting
key_insights: Nvidia's share of the S&P 500 rose from 1% in December 2022 to 8.5% by May this year. Cembalest (JPM) compares the ascent with earlier market leaders GM, IBM, GE and Cisco, most of which lost their dominance. Microsoft and Apple broke that pattern.

NVDA touched its long-term trendline at Thursday's lows and has bounced since the panic open, but the recovery is weak. It trades 22% below its 200-day moving average, versus about 30% below at the Liberation Day lows.

JPM estimates Nvidia captured 83% of AI chip revenues in 2023-2025, with 75% gross margins and 66% operating margins. NVDA now trades at a PEG ratio of 0.2x, the lowest of the major AI names, and still generates strong free cash flow margins, unlike the hyperscalers.

Semiconductors have underperformed the S&P 500 by more than 30 percentage points since June, the largest relative drawdown since 2002. Goldman's AI semiconductor basket trades at 11x 2028 earnings versus nearly 16x for the S&P 500, while consensus expects 31% earnings growth in 2028. At the S&P's multiple, prices would imply roughly a 6% earnings decline.

NDX was rejected at its 200-day moving average. The key level is 27k in NDX futures, a pivot last autumn and the location of the long-term trendline. Equity vols are rising again and the VXN/VIX gap remains wide.
Goldman reports momentum players are near maximum short in NDX. The report says positioning is vulnerable to a sharp reversal.

Vol control and risk parity funds are estimated to have sold more than $30bn combined over the past week because of elevated realized volatility. Goldman notes vol control funds could become meaningful buyers in December/January if volatility settles.
The dollar continues to rise, with little resistance until 105. US yields are moving in its favor and the Fed is turning more hawkish.

Deutsche Bank (Mallika Sachdeva) says Asia's chip trade surpluses are being recycled into US equities rather than Treasuries, unlike the petrodollar era. Foreign equity inflows exceed $1 trillion annually.

Deutsche Bank notes this recycling supports the dollar while financing AI companies, but US equities are three times as volatile as Treasuries and tech stocks up to ten times, so the dollar is increasingly dependent on the AI boom.

Goldman calculates the STOXX Europe 600 has a two-year daily beta below 0.05 to its US AI basket. The report suggests Europe could attract diversification flows, and high, stable-margin European companies are starting to break out.

market_movers.rationale: NVDA is testing its long-term trendline and trades 22% below its 200-day average. JPM cites a 0.2x PEG and 66% operating margins as evidence the valuation reset may be excessive.

sector_views.rationale: Goldman's AI semiconductor basket trades at 11x 2028 earnings versus about 16x for the S&P 500 despite 31% consensus earnings growth, which the report reads as pricing in an earnings decline.
STOXX Europe 600 has a two-year daily beta below 0.05 to the US AI basket, which could draw diversification flows.

earnings_insights: Goldman's AI semiconductor basket trades at 11x 2028 earnings (consensus estimate basis) versus nearly 16x for the S&P 500. Consensus forecasts 31% basket earnings growth in 2028 (estimate, not reported).
JPM estimates Nvidia's gross margin at 75% and operating margin at 66%, with 83% share of AI chip revenues over 2023-2025 (JPM estimate).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Dollar strength is supported by rising US yields and a more hawkish Fed, and increasingly by AI-related equity inflows.
Chip-related surpluses in Asia are recycled into US equities, supporting the dollar and financing AI companies.

risk_factors: Failure of NDX futures at 27k, where the key pivot and long-term trendline sit.
Earnings estimates for AI semiconductors could fall sharply, which would validate the current valuation discount.
Dependence of the dollar on AI-linked equity inflows, given that US equities are three times and tech stocks up to ten times as volatile as Treasuries.
Continued forced selling by systematic funds while realized volatility stays elevated.
vol_and_positioning: Equity vols are spiking again, with the VXN/VIX gap staying wide.
Momentum players are near maximum short in NDX, which the report says leaves positioning vulnerable to a sharp reversal.
Vol control and risk parity funds sold an estimated $30bn+ combined over the past week, and vol control funds could turn buyers in December/January if volatility settles.
